publication_provenance: Primary article DOI and matched full figure pixels. Numeric claims sourced from article text. No overlays allowed inside data figures.

flow-chamber-method.title: What a Bubble Does to a Monolayer
flow-chamber-method.visual_thesis: A published cell-monolayer experiment, not patient airway footage. Flow-device photos, live/dead assay, and actin figure are all the same paper.

headline: THE BUBBLE
PASSES.
scenes.narration: A fluid interface crosses a layer of lung epithelial cells. This is the real chamber study, not a film of a patient's lung.

headline: THE REAL
CHAMBER
scenes.narration: A syringe pump drives liquid through a parallel plate chamber. The paper shows the actual apparatus and the glass surfaces supporting the cells.

headline: WHERE STRESS
APPEARS
scenes.narration: As the air liquid interface advances, local stresses reach the cell surface. The moving schematic explains the process; it is not a measured stress trace.

headline: CONTROL
VERSUS BUBBLE
scenes.narration: These fluorescence images are from the original study. The unstressed control and the bubble exposed cells were stained with live and dead markers.

headline: AROUND 53%
CELL DEATH
scenes.narration: Across seven replicates, the stressed group showed about fifty three percent cell death, versus around zero to point two percent in controls. The difference was statistically significant.

headline: LOOK AGAIN AT
THE ACTIN
scenes.narration: The study also stained actin filaments and nuclei. Here are its actual control and bubble exposure images, not synthetic fluorescence pictures.

headline: NO SIGNIFICANT
ACTIN DIFFERENCE
scenes.narration: The single bubble did not produce a statistically significant change in actin organization, although the authors observed possible differences in filament orientation.

headline: ONE MODEL.
ONE QUESTION.
scenes.eyebrow: PUBLISHED METHOD · NOT A PATIENT OUTCOME
scenes.narration: The chamber makes an airway reopening problem experimentally observable. It does not by itself establish what will happen to a patient during ventilation.

pla-grafting.title: What Changes When PLA Meets Plasma
pla-grafting.visual_thesis: This is the 2021 continuous PLA film/aluminium lamination study, not the distinct 2020 electrospun antimicrobial scaffold paper.

headline: THE PEEL
TELLS THE STORY
scenes.narration: The question was practical: could modifying a plant based PLA film make it adhere more strongly to aluminium? The peel test would give the answer.

headline: ACTIVATE
THE SURFACE
scenes.narration: Cold plasma changes the outermost polymer surface, creating reactive sites. The study then grafted ascorbic or fumaric acid onto the treated PLA film.

headline: WHAT WATER
REVEALS
scenes.eyebrow: FIGURE 1 · CONTACT ANGLE AND SURFACE ENERGY
scenes.narration: The authors measured contact angles and surface free energy. Both help characterize wetting, but neither measurement alone proves stronger laminate adhesion.

headline: CHEMISTRY
AT THE SURFACE
scenes.narration: The X ray photoelectron spectra belong to this exact PLA film paper. They help characterize the chemistry of the surface after the treatments.

headline: THE PEEL
EXPERIMENT
scenes.narration: This published figure compares peel resistance of untreated PLA, plasma treated samples, grafted samples, and blind controls without plasma activation.

headline: TO 211 N/m
scenes.narration: Untreated film averaged seventy four point four newtons per metre. The fumaric acid grafted sample reached two hundred eleven newtons per metre, the largest increase.

headline: THE CONTROL
CHANGES THE CLAIM
scenes.eyebrow: NO PLASMA · NO COMPARABLE ADHESION GAIN
scenes.narration: Adding the acids without prior plasma treatment gave results close to untreated film. That blind control is central to how the researchers interpreted grafting.

headline: FILM IS NOT
SCAFFOLD
scenes.narration: These results describe PLA film and aluminium peel adhesion. They must not be illustrated with the separate twenty twenty antimicrobial electrospun scaffold experiment.

ace2-covid-drugs.title: Soluble ACE2 Is Not a Treatment Verdict
ace2-covid-drugs.visual_thesis: The exact 2022 observational hypertensive COVID-19 paper, with its published circulating ACE2/angiotensin-II figures. No third-party 2021 review graphics, patient photos, or causal claims.

headline: TWO BLOOD
MARKERS
scenes.narration: This clinical study measured circulating ACE two and angiotensin two in two hundred hypertensive patients with COVID nineteen. It is an observational analysis, not a treatment trial.

headline: SEVERITY
AND ACE TWO
scenes.narration: The original dot plots compare circulating ACE two and angiotensin two across mild, moderate, and severe illness, with the authors' reported confidence intervals.

headline: HIGHER IN
SEVERE CASES
scenes.narration: The reported soluble ACE two level was about one point nine times higher in severe disease than in mild cases. This does not establish the direction of causation.

headline: FOUR MEDICINE
CLASSES
scenes.narration: The researchers compared patients taking ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers. These were recorded exposures, not randomly assigned drugs.

headline: REAL ASSAY
DISTRIBUTIONS
scenes.narration: The original figure shows variation between medication groups in circulating ACE two and angiotensin two. These are blood assays, not direct measurements of membrane receptor expression.

headline: GROUPS AND
ILLNESS SEVERITY
scenes.narration: The third figure separates medication classes by disease severity. It reports treatment group associations within an already ill population, not clinical benefit from starting a drug.

headline: ASSOCIATION
IS NOT CAUSE
scenes.narration: Medication choice, baseline cardiovascular disease, age, and illness severity can all shape the observed associations. The study cannot resolve all of those differences.

headline: MEASURED
NOT PRESCRIBED
scenes.narration: The contribution is a clinical biochemical observation linking treatment context, soluble ACE two, and angiotensin two. It does not tell a patient to change medication.
